title: The sharp tongue
hookLine: Kabir mocked empty ritual at the mosque, at the temple, and in his own prayer beads
tomorrow: she tied a knot for each insult. why did her cloths weigh the same?

cards: The church is full, Hannah is walking down the aisle, and Theo's cousin leans over during the opening prayer to mutter a joke about the God stuff. Zoe almost laughs.
Kabir would have had something to say, and he'd have said it to everyone in the room. Now go back to his own city. Kabir stops under a mosque as the call to prayer rings out from the top.
You piled up pebbles and stones to build this, he says, and the mullah climbs up and shouts. Has God gone deaf?

teach.b: Then he turns to worship before images of stone. If God is found by worshiping a stone, he says, I'll worship a whole mountain. Better the grinding stone at home: the world eats the flour it grinds.
And then he turns on his own practice. Kabir's own path is remembering God's name, and many who remember it count on a mala, a string of beads.

teach.h: THE BEADS TURN; THE MIND WANDERS.
teach.b: The beads turn in the hand, he says, the tongue turns in the mouth, and the mind wanders off in every direction. That isn't remembering. So who did Kabir mock hardest?
Whoever was going through the motions, and that included people doing exactly what he taught.
Here's the teaching under the sharp tongue: for Kabir, the form isn't the worship. What counts is the heart turned toward God.
A shout from a tower, a stone in a shrine, a bead in his own hand can all carry that, or all be empty. His target in these couplets is the motion without the heart. He mocked the empty.
Which brings it back to the pew.

teach.h: A SNEER CAN BE EMPTY TOO.
teach.b: Kabir would have aimed at the cousin's joke too: a sneer on autopilot is its own empty ritual.
And three rows up, Theo stood and read his sister's passage, meaning every word.

how: Kabir's sharp dohas against empty ritual are sung in bhajan gatherings and quoted as a check on one's own practice; in the Kabir Panth, remembering the name inwardly is valued above outward forms.

games.q: your friend says grace before every meal, then scrolls through it. she asks if Kabir would tell her to stop. what fits?
o: yes: rituals are empty, so drop grace altogether
no: Kabir only criticized other people's rituals
no: keep it, and mean it; the motion alone is empty
games.why: Kabir aimed at his own beads too. the form can carry a turned heart, or be empty; the point is the meaning.

practice: Pick one small thing you say or do every day without thinking: a thank you, a grace before eating, a goodnight. Do it now, once, slowly, meaning every word. Then sit with the difference between the motion and the meaning.

wordCard.voice: The sharp tongue: Kabir's mockery of empty ritual in every camp, his own included, aimed at the motion without the heart.

orig.note: Hindi and Sanskrit: a string of beads for remembering God's name; Kabir's couplet turns on it.

carryVoice: Keep this one: mocking the empty, never the one who means it. Eight days, and the weaver's song is done.
